## Totals

| | |
|---|---|
| Registers declared | 136 (2 simulation only) |
| Fields declared | 279 |
| Float aliases (`+0x080`) | 30 |
| Command streams | 5 |
| PciFifo decode entries (`getCategories`) | 158 |
| …of which FIFO=Yes / Sync=Yes / FIFO=No | 143 / 71 / 15 |

Categories are `voodoo.bus.RegisterCategory`: `fifoNoSync` (FIFO=Yes, Sync=No),
`fifoWithSync` (FIFO=Yes, Sync=Yes) and `bypassFifo` (FIFO=No). A register with
no category entry — `status` and the five statistics counters, declared with
the plain `newRegAt` — falls through PciFifo's default and behaves as FIFO=No
(`PciFifo.scala:456`).

The **float alias** column gives the IEEE-754 single-precision alias address
(`target + 0x080`) and the arithmetic right shift applied after conversion:
PciFifo converts to a fixed `SQ(50, 30)` intermediate with
`Fpxx2AFix(20 bits, 30 bits, float32)` and then shifts by `30 - fracBits`,
rounding a negative result up when any bit is shifted out
(`PciFifo.floatCorrected`).

## Cross-check against `ext/SpinalVoodoo/docs/sst-1.md`

The datasheet's section 5 register table (remapping disabled) lists
162 register addresses. Comparing them with the table above —
registers plus float-alias addresses:

### In the datasheet, not implemented

| Address | Datasheet name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `0x204` | `vRetrace` | not implemented by the upstream core |

### Implemented, not in the datasheet's section 5 table

| Address | Name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `0x240` | `debugBusy` | simulation-only debug register |
| `0x244` | `fbiInit5` | reserved in the SST-1 map; implemented here as a Voodoo 2 / V2+ register |
| `0x248` | `fbiInit6` | reserved in the SST-1 map; implemented here as a Voodoo 2 / V2+ register |
| `0x24c` | `fbiInit7` | reserved in the SST-1 map; implemented here as a Voodoo 2 / V2+ register |
| `0x250` | `writePathDebug` | simulation-only debug register |

Everything else matches address for address, including the 30 float aliases at
`0x088`–`0x0fc`, the 32 two-entry `fogTable` words at `0x160`–`0x1dc` and the
two 12-word NCC tables at `0x324`–`0x380`.

Field-level deviations worth knowing (the datasheet's "Bits" column is the
architectural width; RegisterBank often declares the full 32 bits):

- `texBaseAddr`, `texBaseAddr_1`, `texBaseAddr_2`, `texBaseAddr_3_8` are
  declared 24 bits wide; the datasheet defines bits `[18:0]`, and only those
  reach `TexLayoutTables` / `CoreCpuFrontdoor`.
- `fbzMode` and `lfbMode` declare their upper bits as an explicit RW
  `reserved` field (`[31:21]` and `[31:17]`), so they read back what was
  written rather than as undefined.
- `clipLeftRight` / `clipLowYHighY` reset their right/bottom boundary to
  `0x3ff` (the datasheet leaves reset values unspecified).
- `startR` / `startG` / `startB` reset to `255 << 12` rather than 0.
- `fbiInit1.videoTilesX` resets to 10 (a 640-pixel stride).

## Address-decode quirks

- PCI BAR split (CoreCpuFrontdoor.scala:22-27): cpuAddr[23:22] selects 0 = register set (0x000000-0x3fffff), 1 = LFB (0x400000-0x7fffff), 2 and 3 = texture memory (0x800000-0xffffff). Texture writes are pushed into the same PCI FIFO as register writes, tagged isTexture.
- chip-select field: the datasheet divides the 22-bit register address into wrap[21:14] / chip[13:10] / register[9:2] / byte[1:0] (sst-1.md section 5). CoreCpuFrontdoor.scala:36 rebuilds the address as cpuAddr[21:14] ## 4'b0000 ## cpuAddr[9:0], i.e. it *forces the chip field to zero*. Every chip selector therefore aliases onto the same register, which is what a single-FBI + single-TREX implementation wants.
- texture-register mirrors: because of the zeroed chip field there is only one copy of the TREX registers (0x300-0x380). On real hardware those are mirrored per TREX chip and the chip field picks which ones are written; here a write addressed at TREX #1 or #2 lands on the one TMU register set.
- wrap field: bits [20:14] survive into the 22-bit external bus but are then truncated by AddressRemapper (AddressRemapper.scala:95-99 resize to 12 bits), so all 256 wraps alias. Bit 21 is the exception: it selects the RGBZASTW remap (see REMAP_TABLE) and is cleared for everything else.
- the register file therefore only ever sees 10 significant address bits (0x000-0x3fc) even though the BMB port is 12 bits wide (RegisterBank.scala:1258).
- 0x128 (swapbufferCMD) is wired to PciFifo.io.wasEnqueuedAddr in Core.scala:210; PciFifo raises wasEnqueued when a non-texture write to it is pushed into the FIFO (PciFifo.scala:270), and Core feeds that to SwapBuffer and back into RegisterBank as swapCmdEnqueued.
- texBaseAddr relocation: CPU reads of texture memory are offset by texBaseAddr[18:0] << 3 (CoreCpuFrontdoor.scala:46-48); CPU writes are not, they carry the raw 23-bit PCI offset.
- addresses with no entry in the category map (status, the five statistics counters, and every hole in the map) default to fifoBypass = True in PciFifo (PciFifo.scala:456), so they are never queued.
